_readme: Noul questions for Jev (TypeSafe System One). 'yes_means' tells code how to read p(yes): 'concern' = a high value is a problem, 'ok' = a high value is good, 'info' = a fact that other checks combine with. Thresholds are starting points: validate on your own data before trusting them (see --validate).

commit.source: handbook 05 §1 (git log -p must never show a real key)
commit.instructions: Does this commit add a literal credential (API key, token, password or secret) that looks real, as opposed to an empty value, an env() lookup without a literal default, or an obvious placeholder?

criteria.true: A value shaped like a real credential appears in added lines, including as a default argument or inside an example env file. A SECRET-LIKE marker counts as a real-looking value.
criteria.false: Only empty values, env() references without a literal default, or clearly fake placeholders such as changeme or xxx.

commit.source: handbook 06 §1 + DoD 07 (new package/pattern/contract needs an ADR before the code lands)
commit.instructions: Does this commit introduce a new third-party package, external service integration, or architectural pattern to the repository, beyond routine use of what already exists?

criteria.true: A new composer or npm dependency, a new outbound API client, or a new cross-cutting mechanism such as a shared response envelope or a limiter registry.
criteria.false: Routine feature, fix, refactor, docs or test work using packages and patterns already in the repo.

commit.instructions: Does this commit add business or integration behavior under the root app/ directory instead of inside an owning module?

criteria.true: Services, API clients, validation rules or domain logic placed in app/, other than the User model, service providers, or console kernel code.
criteria.false: Changes live inside Modules/, or only touch kernel files, docs, config, tests or tooling.

commit.source: handbook 03 §4 (flaky tests are defects) + CI runs in-memory SQLite with no secrets
commit.instructions: Does a test added or changed in this commit depend on a real external service, a real network call, or a real API key instead of a fake?

criteria.true: The test would fail offline or without a secret, for example it calls a live HTTP API without Http::fake().
criteria.false: No test is touched, or every touched test runs against fakes, factories and the in-memory database only.

commit.source: handbook 03 §2 (every cited RULE needs a test naming it)
commit.instructions: Does this commit change behavior that a numbered business rule or SCOPE item in the spec governs (RULE-xxx or SCOPE-xxx)?

criteria.true: Changes enrollment, course lifecycle, grading, delegation, approval, or another behavior that a spec rule constrains.
criteria.false: Scaffolding, tooling, docs, formatting or infrastructure with no business-rule behavior.

commit.source: handbook 01 §5 + todo.md (phases strictly in order; ModulesSmokeTest gate)
commit.instructions: Does this commit implement functionality that belongs to a phase later than repo_context.current_phase?

criteria.true: Adds endpoints, tables or services whose phase appears after the current phase in repo_context.phases.
criteria.false: The work belongs to the current or an earlier phase, or is docs or tooling that supports them.

commit.source: handbook 01 §3 (one task = one PR) + 04 §4 (no unrelated changes)
commit.instructions: Does this commit combine unrelated changes that would normally be separate commits, for example a feature plus unrelated tooling or dependency changes?

criteria.true: Two or more independent purposes are visible in the commit message or in the changed files.
criteria.false: One coherent purpose, even if it touches several files.

rule.instructions: Does the rule text explicitly require database-level enforcement (for example the words DB-enforced, unique, or a constraint), as opposed to application-level enforcement or no enforcement?

criteria.true: The rule states or clearly implies that the database must enforce it.
criteria.false: The rule is application-enforced, is silent about enforcement, or forbids a constraint.

rule.instructions: Does the supplied migration enforce this rule with a database constraint (unique index, foreign key or check) instead of leaving it only to application code?

criteria.true: A unique index, foreign key or check constraint in the migration directly enforces the rule.
criteria.false: The migration only stores the data; enforcement would have to happen in application code.

rule.instructions: Does the supplied migration contradict the rule text, for example a missing column, uniqueness on the wrong columns, or a constraint the rule says must not exist?

criteria.true: The migration's structure conflicts with what the rule requires or forbids.
criteria.false: The migration is consistent with the rule, or the rule does not constrain the schema.
